meat: Pulpo á feira, lacón con grelos, empanada — usually tuna or pork.
veg: Pimientos de Padrón, tortilla, cachelos, tetilla cheese, grelos.
verdict: Seafood is the religion and pork is the fallback. The padrón peppers are a starter, not a dinner.

meat: Fabada (chorizo, morcilla and lacón), cachopo, cider-house sausage.
veg: Cabrales, tortilla, pisto, and the odd pixín-free salad.
verdict: The bean stew everyone tells you to try is about forty per cent pig. Asturias is hard work.

meat: Cocido montañés, anchoas de Santoña, rabas.
veg: Tortilla, ensalada, quesada and sobaos — none of which is dinner.
verdict: Even the cabbage stew has pork in it. The dairy is superb, which helps more than you would think.

meat: Txuleta, bacalao al pil-pil, kokotxas, morcilla.
veg: Pintxos of tortilla, piquillos, hongos a la plancha, Idiazábal.
verdict: Pintxo bars let you graze around the meat, and San Sebastián has kitchens that mean it.

meat: Chistorra, lamb, and jamón as a garnish on everything.
veg: Menestra de Tudela, white asparagus, piquillo peppers, alcachofas, borraja.
verdict: Spain's vegetable garden. The menestra is still finished with jamón unless you say otherwise — so say otherwise.

meat: Patatas a la riojana with chorizo, chuletillas al sarmiento.
veg: Menestra riojana, pochas, peppers, wild mushrooms.
verdict: Serious vegetable cooking exists here. The default potatoes still have chorizo cooked into them.

meat: Ternasco, migas with panceta, jamón de Teruel.
veg: Borraja, cardo, menestra if you ask twice.
verdict: Lamb country. The borage and cardoon are excellent and nobody will ever suggest them to you.

meat: Cocido madrileño, callos, bocadillo de calamares.
veg: The second-best veg scene in Spain, and every other cuisine on earth.
verdict: The traditional dish is three courses of pig, but it is a capital city — you will eat well regardless.

meat: Lechazo, cochinillo, morcilla de Burgos, cecina, jamón.
veg: Sopa de ajo if it was not made with ham, pisto, judiones.
verdict: The hardest region in Spain. Asking for something vegetarian gets you a plate of ham, and they mean it kindly.

meat: Migas, perdiz, and gazpacho manchego — a game stew, not a soup.
veg: Pisto manchego, queso manchego, berenjenas de Almagro.
verdict: Pisto is a genuinely great vegetable dish. Almost everything else has something shot in it.

meat: Jamón ibérico de bellota, migas extremeñas, caldereta de cordero.
veg: Torta del Casar, patatas with pimentón, tomato and cheese.
verdict: The acorn-fed pig is the entire point of the region. Come for the cheese and manage expectations.

meat: Botifarra amb mongetes, fricandó, canelons.
veg: Escalivada, calçots in season, espinacs a la catalana, pa amb tomàquet, trinxat.
verdict: Escalivada alone justifies the trip, and Barcelona has the best vegetarian scene in the country.

meat: Paella valenciana is rabbit and chicken. Embutido everywhere else.
veg: Paella de verduras is traditional rather than a concession. Horchata, esgarraet if you eat fish.
verdict: The rice can be entirely vegetable and nobody blinks. The best-fed region on this map.

meat: Sobrasada on everything, frit mallorquí, porcella.
veg: Tumbet, trampó, pa amb oli, coca de verdures.
verdict: Sobrasada gets on everything it can, but tumbet is a proper dish and the resort kitchens cater.

meat: Jamón, rabo de toro, pescaíto frito.
veg: Gazpacho, salmorejo, pisto, espinacas con garbanzos, berenjenas con miel, alboronía.
verdict: Tapas culture means small vegetable dishes everywhere. Only the ham on the salmorejo betrays you.

meat: Michirones with ham and chorizo, marinera with its anchovy.
veg: Zarangollo, pisto murciano, alcachofas, tomate huevera, paparajotes.
verdict: The market garden of Europe. Order zarangollo and stop worrying about it.

meat: Cordero, pinchos morunos.
veg: North African salads, couscous de verduras, chickpeas.
verdict: The Moroccan influence widens the field considerably, which the mainland could learn from.

meat: Cordero, pinchos morunos, tagines with lamb.
veg: Couscous de verduras, salads, chickpea stews, mint tea.
verdict: Same story as Ceuta: the closer to Morocco, the easier the vegetables get.

meat: Conejo en salmorejo, carne de cabra, ropa vieja.
veg: Papas arrugadas con mojo, gofio escaldado, potaje de verduras, almogrote.
verdict: The potatoes and mojo are vegetarian by nature, and the potajes usually are — right up until they are not.

meat: Francesinha, tripas à moda do Porto, caldo verde with its chouriço.
veg: Broa, grão de bico, caldo verde with the sausage left out.
verdict: Porto's signature dish is a sandwich buried under meat and sauce. The city has vegetarian kitchens; the region does not.

meat: Cataplana, sardinhas, carne de porco à alentejana.
veg: Salada de tomate, favas, bread and cheese.
verdict: Fish everywhere, and the tourist strip will make you an omelette. Little else is on offer.

meat: Leitão da Bairrada and chanfana, which is goat.
veg: Sopa de legumes, migas, broa.
verdict: Bairrada exists to roast a piglet. The vegetable soup is genuinely good and genuinely all there is.

meat: Bacalhau in a thousand forms, bifana, cozido.
veg: A real vegetarian scene, açorda, and every market stall in the city.
verdict: A capital with actual vegetarian restaurants, marooned in a country built on salt cod.

meat: Choco frito, bifanas, grilled fish off the boat.
veg: Tomato salad, queijo de Azeitão, bread.
verdict: Setúbal fries cuttlefish and does it beautifully. That is the whole menu.

meat: Porco preto, ensopado de borrego, açorda finished with bacon.
veg: Açorda alentejana of bread, garlic and coriander. Gaspacho alentejano, migas.
verdict: The bread-and-garlic soups are peasant food and vegetarian almost by accident. Check about the bacon.

meat: Sopa da pedra, leitão, grilled fish.
veg: Vegetable soups, bread, pêra rocha and the market gardens behind them.
verdict: Market-garden country whose restaurants have not noticed yet.

meat: Cozido das Furnas, cooked in volcanic soil and entirely animal. Beef in all directions.
veg: Pineapple, cheese, and soup.
verdict: An island of cattle. The famous stew is buried in the ground for six hours and comes out full of pork.

meat: Espetada on a bay laurel skewer, lapas, black scabbardfish.
veg: Bolo do caco with garlic butter, sopa de trigo, and the fruit.
verdict: The garlic flatbread is the best vegetarian thing on the island, which tells you where you stand.
